newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Ag Min soybean crop estimate expected soon.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Ag Min soybean crop estimate expected soon.

text.p: Brazil's Agriculture Ministry is likely to issue on October 29 its first estimate of the 1996/97 soybean crop, which is expected to be below other forecasts, an Agriculture Ministry official said.
"Most people are anticipating a 13 percent increase from last year to around 26 million tonnes," the official said.
"But probably our estimate will see about half of this increase, say of around 1.5 million tonnes to 24.50 million tonnes," the official said.

A team of agronomists from the Agriculture Ministry's National Supply Company have recently returned from a field trip of the soybean regions where the principal problem facing farmers is seen to be credit to buy seeds and necessary inputs.
"Because of the prevailing conditions, our estimates are not so optimistic," the official said.
"The crop should certainly be bigger than last year ...but it will be hard for us to reach 26 million tonnes if credit problems are not resolved," the official said.
Independent analysts Safras e Mercado are working with a forecast of 25.89 million tonnes in the coming year, based on planting intentions, against 23.05 million tonnes in 1995/96.
Earlier this month, the U.S. Department of Agriculture left its estimate for Brazil unchanged at 26 million tonnes.
One region where the outlook is more optimistic than earlier anticipated is Mato Grosso where some farmers had expected to see a sharp drop in output due to severe financial problems.
However planted area is now seen as virtually equalling last year's 1.85 million hectares which produced 4.5 million tonnes, the official said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
